sites.name: Governance and Secretariat
sites.description: Council and Senate papers, University policies and procedures, information governance, and corporate templates.
sites.hint: The rules are kept here: the AI Acceptable Use Policy, the Data Classification Scheme and the naming convention among them. Most of the other exercises use these as the ruleset, so it is worth reading them first. You will then be able to see how much of the rest of the Hub ignores them.

sites.name: Faculty of Health and Education
sites.description: Faculty office, Departments of Health and Education, programme teaching materials, and the migrated StoneShare drive.
sites.hint: The biggest site and the untidiest. The Dean's Office is where briefings land and drafts go wrong. The StoneShare Migration library is the old network drive, dropped here in November 1052 and never sorted; it holds things that should not be in a shared library at all. It is the place to start for the folder- organisation and guardrails exercises.

sites.name: Programme Support Team Nursing and Care
sites.folder: Programme Support Team Nursing and Care
sites.description: Administrative team for the Nursing and Care programme: placements, provider liaison, student records and programme administration.
sites.hint: Placements for the largest programme in the Faculty are run from a spreadsheet with fourteen tabs by one person, who goes on leave in May. Everything you would need to scope a small system is here in pieces: the spreadsheet itself, the complaints about it, the provider letters, and the form Digital Services rejected two years ago. Use this site for project management and for pulling a table out of a pile of correspondence.

sites.name: Planning and Insight
sites.description: Institutional data, analysis and reporting. Student numbers, awarding gaps, NSS, surveys, data requests.
sites.hint: This team owns the numbers. Their Reports library is the one place in the Hub where the naming convention is followed, and it shows. The Data Extracts are small cuts of the full Stonegrove dataset, which you can download from the main site. In the Working folder there is a half-finished awarding gap analysis and two summaries that a tool generated and nobody checked.

sites.name: Quality
sites.description: Academic regulations, programme approval and revalidation, examination boards, external examining.
sites.hint: The formal register. Regulations here are written to be quoted rather than read, which makes them good practice for turning into plain guidance. The Occupational Therapy revalidation folder has a panel transcript, the minutes the clerk produced from it, and a reserved item that must stay out of the open minutes.

sites.name: Admissions
sites.description: Applicant processing, offer-making, conversion, open days and applicant communications for the 1053 entry cycle.
sites.hint: Offers are up and acceptances are down, and there are three explanations in three documents, each written for a different audience. The applicant tracker holds more personal data than it needs and is labelled Internal. Someone has also pasted an applicant's personal statement into a tool that is not on the approved list. A good site for the guardrails exercise and for drafting in the right voice.

sites.name: Student Wellbeing
sites.description: Disability support, mental health and wellbeing advice, reasonable adjustments, and student casework.
sites.hint: Support plans and case notes are labelled correctly here. The trouble is the copies that have ended up elsewhere. Start in the Incident folder and trace the February incident to where the file actually went. Useful for the guardrails exercise and for drafting a difficult email.

sites.name: Communications
sites.description: Brand, design, campaigns, internal and external communications, requests for communications support.
sites.hint: The brand guide is here, along with the Brand Compliance Log, a spreadsheet of every off-brand sighting since the 1051 rebrand. Give an AI the guide and ask for a set of materials, then point it at the off-brand files scattered across the other sites and see whether it keeps to the rules.
